title: Möbius zero-mask rule against a solved LP2 page
question: Does the reported Möbius-of-totient zero-preservation rule hold under the published LP2-56 decoding?
summary: On 85 LP2-56 runes, the known one-step subtraction changes zero to nonzero at 28 positions. The proposed one-way invariant therefore does not generalize to known Liber Primus decoding.

scope.representation: All 85 GP runes in the archived page, with φ(p)=p−1 and μ(φ(p)) evaluated on each GP prime; plaintext index is cipher index minus one modulo 29.
scope.procedure: Count one-way and reverse zero-mask violations under the published shift; enumerate all 29 constant shifts as a calculation comparison and independently check zero by square divisors.
scope.parameters: 29 GP symbols; 85 page runes; shifts 0–28; reported necessary direction is ciphertext μ=0 implies plaintext μ=0.
scope.exclusions: The proposed LP2-00 candidate sentence, its semantic ranking and word list, other cipher families, proof against a page-specific rule, and significance of a post-selected phrase.

finding: The published LP2-56 shift has 28 zero-to-nonzero violations, 22 reverse changes and 50 total mask mismatches among 85 runes.
limitations: A counterexample to a universal decoding invariant is not a refutation of a separately specified LP2-00-only mechanism. The report’s LP2-00 word-selection step remains unreplayed.
next_steps: Pin the original LP2-00 code, dictionary and exact proposed plaintext, then compare the whole candidate count and an untouched continuation against controls.

review.reviewer: Codex; independent square-divisor and rune-stream check; human review pending

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12 standard library; independent check with check.py
